xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5094: Lane launches ignore the disk floor and superseded lanes are never reaped (31 lanes / ~45 GiB in one morning)

plan.title: Lane launches ignore the disk floor and superseded lanes are never reaped (31 lanes / ~45 GiB in one morning)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: A gauntlet run created 31 lane folders (~45 GiB) in one morning and reaped none; free space hit 17 MB. The lane doors (launchLane, launchOwnedLane) never call the PAN-4961 disk floor, nothing tells an orchestrator which lanes a newer iteration superseded, and 24 of the 29 folders were worktrees the orchestrator created itself with git worktree add, which no door sees.
narratives.Proposal: Both lane doors admit the disk floor through a new src/lib/lanes/disk.ts (reserveDiskFloor at the lanes root, new-worktree bytes from the workspace host estimate, 0 for --reuse/play, HTTP 507 code disk-low, --force no bypass, the owner checks remote lanes). A pure rule (src/lib/lanes/reapable.ts) gives every LaneView reapable/supersededBy; pan lane list shows a REAPABLE column and --reapable filter, and pan lane wait prints the reapable lanes after a report. A local pan lane disk-check verb previews the floor and lists non-lane directories under the lanes root. The pan-lane and pan-gauntlet-loop skills and reference/lanes.mdx teach: check the disk before every wave and self-made worktree, reap superseded lanes before the next iteration, remove self-made worktrees.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to src/lib/disk-floor.ts (threshold, refusal text, ledger).
- No low-disk operator alert or phone push (PAN-5093 owns that backstop).
- No server-side automatic reaping and no bulk pan lane reap verb.
- No change to reapLane semantics (it never kills and never discards work).
- Overdeck never removes unregistered directories; disk-check only lists them.
- No interception of raw git worktree add or Agent-tool worktree isolation.
- No dashboard UI for reapable; the Awareness rail card is unchanged.
- No reapable hint in MCP lane_wait; MCP lane_status returns the new view fields as-is.
- No new HTTP route and no no-loss-matrix row.
- --force must not bypass the disk floor.

autoDecisions.summary: Refuse a lane below the floor with HTTP 507 and code 'disk-low'
autoDecisions.rationale: container-ops.ts already answers 507 for the same disk-floor refusal; a code gives the skill a machine-readable signal. Only the LaneLaunchError union and OWNER_STATUSES need 507.
The issue asks for the same 'Disk low' message and free GiB; disk-floor.ts stays untouched.

autoDecisions.summary: Estimate a new lane worktree as estimateWorkspaceDiskCost(project).hostBytes
autoDecisions.rationale: Builder lanes install dependencies in their own worktree, so tracked bytes plus an unshared node_modules matches the ~1.4 GiB incident lanes; it shares the workspace memo and overestimates sparse lanes, the safe direction.

autoDecisions.summary: --reuse and play launches reserve 0 bytes but are still floor-checked
autoDecisions.rationale: They create no worktree, yet a new agent writes to disk; nothing new should start below the floor.
CPU saturation is recoverable; ENOSPC zero-fills files (PAN-1674). lane_start over MCP strips force anyway.

autoDecisions.summary: Reapable is decided per iteration group, excludes orchestrator lanes, and judges wait for a newer judge iteration
autoDecisions.rationale: --reuse rows share a directory; an archived orchestrator orphans its lanes; a builder of the next iteration reads the critic's verdict file inside the critic's worktree.

autoDecisions.summary: Nudge through pan lane list --reapable and a stderr hint after pan lane wait reports, not server-side auto-reap or a bulk reap verb
autoDecisions.rationale: Reaping stays explicit and safe (reapLane never discards work); the orchestrator sees the hint on every loop turn.

autoDecisions.summary: Cover self-made worktrees with a local `pan lane disk-check` verb plus gauntlet-skill rules, with PAN-5093 as the backstop
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue comment names this path: 24 of 29 folders were raw git worktree add, which no door can intercept. A local verb needs no new route or no-loss-matrix row.

autoDecisions.summary: disk-check lists unregistered directories under the lanes root but never removes them
autoDecisions.rationale: Overdeck cannot know whether a directory it did not create holds unpushed work; git worktree remove refuses a dirty tree.

autoDecisions.summary: Leave the codebase map out of this plan's files
autoDecisions.rationale: Adding it would make a seventh subsystem and fail the projected-surface lint; the map is refreshed by /pan-map and nothing in it is stale.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4. Create src/lib/lanes/reapable.ts with ReapableRow and supersededLanes(rows) exactly as the PRD snippet: group by (run, key, role), skip orchestrator, and for every iteration below the group's highest, flag all non-archived rows when none is working/needs-you/starting and either some row of the iteration reported or no non-archived row is idle; map each to the name of the newest (latest createdAt) row of the highest iteration. Write src/lib/lanes/__tests__/reapable.test.ts with one case per bullet in the PRD.

items.title: Given builder i1 idle and reported and builder i2 working, supersededLanes returns a map with i1 -> i2's name and no entry for i2
Given i1 working (reported), or i1 idle without a report, plus i2, supersededLanes returns no entry for i1; given i1 stopped without a report plus i2, it returns i1
Given two --reuse rows in i1 (one stopped and reported, one working) plus i2, it returns neither; when both are stopped it returns both mapped to i2
Given critic i1 reported and builder i2 but no critic i2, it returns nothing; after critic i2 exists it returns critic i1; orchestrator i1 with orchestrator i2 never appears
Given archived rows, a single iteration, or groups of different run or key, supersededLanes returns no entry for them
